chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about the one who raises his head before the Imam. Should he return and bow if the Imam is delayed in raising his head? He (peace be upon him) said: No.
ai.seo_question: What should a worshipper do if he raises his head from ruku' before the Imam?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Al-Kafi* by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the principle of *tardud* (returning) in congregational prayer, ruling that a follower who prematurely rises from *ruku'* need not return to it if the Imam delays, thereby preserving the validity of the prayer without redundancy. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on the follower's alignment with the Imam's pace while maintaining the structural integrity of the prayer units. It serves as a practical guideline for congregants to avoid unnecessary movements when the Imam's timing varies slightly.
